title: When “idle” isn't idle: how a Linux kernel optimization became a QUIC bug
summary: Cloudflare engineers discovered how a Linux kernel optimization for handling TCP 'idle' timeout semantics inadvertently broke QUIC protocol implementations, causing connections to fail in unexpected ways. The bug originated from misaligned assumptions between kernel-level TCP behavior and QUIC's own idle timeout mechanisms.
problem_solved: This case study reveals and explains a subtle but critical networking bug where Linux kernel optimizations designed for TCP conflicted with QUIC protocol expectations, leading to connection failures.
why_valuable: It provides a real-world example of how low-level kernel optimizations can unexpectedly break higher-level protocol implementations, serving as a cautionary tale for developers working across system layers.
